baseImageKnown.description: False when the base image was not identified: every finding was attributed to the build, so `baseImage` counted nothing.

fixable.description: Introduced by this build, with a published fix. On a fresh database a build with any is refused.

unfixable.description: Introduced by this build, with no published fix: recorded, not blocking.

baseImage.description: The base image’s own — the blueprint’s to fix.

unfixableFindings.description: The unfixable findings by id, at most 50; `unfixable` counts them all.

id.description: The vulnerability’s id — a CVE or an advisory.

package.description: The package it is in, with its version.

SensitiveDiff.description: Which sensitive fields this manifest changes against the project’s newest VALID one. Reported here, and enforced at a launched app’s production deploy, where such a change needs an administrator’s approval.

fields.description: Which of them changed — `services`, `auth.attributes`, `egress.allow` and so on.

SetAppSecretRequest.description: The value to store under the name in the path.

value.description: The value, as text: at least 6 characters (a shorter one could not be redacted from the app’s Incidents), at most 16384 bytes of UTF-8, well-formed, with no NUL. Takes effect at the next deploy of this environment; it is never answered back.

SlugCheck.description: Whether a slug is available: exactly what project creation will answer — advisory, since creation checks again.

reasons.description: Present when `available` is false: every reason that applies.

code.description: The code `createProject` would refuse it with.

message.description: What is wrong with it, for a person.

SourceFile.description: One file at one commit, whole — as text, or as base64 bytes.

ref.description: A branch name, or a full 40-character commit id. Defaults to `main`.

commitSha.description: The commit the file was read at.

path.description: The file’s path from the repository root.

content.description: The file’s content, whole: its text exactly (`encoding: utf8`, at most 1 MiB), or its bytes as canonical base64 (`encoding: base64`, at most 2 MiB decoded).

encoding.description: How `content` carries the file: `utf8` — text, the default read — or `base64`, when the read asked for `encoding=base64`.

mode.description: `100644`, or `100755` for an executable file — kept when the file is changed.

blobSha.description: git's id for this content; equal ids mean equal bytes.

SourceTree.description: Every path in the repository at one commit — the files an API client can read and write.

ref.description: A branch name, or a full 40-character commit id. Defaults to `main`.

commitSha.description: The commit the ref resolved to — what this listing is OF. Send it as `baseCommit` when committing changes computed from it.

entries.description: Every entry of the tree, sorted by path.

path.description: The path from the repository root, `/`-separated.

type.description: What git records at this path. The API reads and writes `file`s only.

mode.description: git's mode: `100644` a file, `100755` an executable file, `120000` a symlink, `040000` a directory, `160000` a submodule.

size.description: Bytes, for a file or a symlink; null otherwise.

binary.description: Whether git calls this file binary — read it with `getFile`’s `encoding=base64`. An image, PDF or font (the ten kinds `createCommit` writes as bytes) can be written back with `encoding: base64`; any other binary file only by a push. Null for anything that is not a file.

truncated.description: True when the tree has more than 10,000 entries and only the first 10,000, by path, are listed.

Spec.description: The project’s newest recorded validation of manifest.yaml, parsed, when it is valid — an invalid one is answered `422 SPEC_INVALID` instead. Its commit is the one a build names when it names none.

commitSha.description: The commit whose manifest.yaml it is.

spec.description: manifest.yaml v1 as parsed and validated, every default filled in. `ManifestYaml` in this document describes each field.

SpecValidation.description: One validation of manifest.yaml at one commit, recorded — valid or not — and announced as `spec.validated`.

commitSha.description: The commit whose manifest.yaml was validated.

valid.description: Whether it is valid; a build of this commit needs it to be.

errors.description: Every problem, each with its path and code; empty when `valid`.

warnings.description: What the validation says WITHOUT refusing — a field validated and recorded but not enforced yet (`SPEC_FIELD_NOT_ENFORCED`). Never a reason `valid` is false; empty for a manifest that did not parse. Show them where the errors are shown.

StartAgentSessionRequest.description: What an agent session is for, and — optionally — less than the platform’s cap or life.

name.description: A label a person reads in the list of sessions — the task the agent is on.

capUsd.description: The most this session may spend, in US dollars: the platform’s session cap when absent — and never more than it, nor than what remains of your month.

durationMinutes.description: How long the key lives: 60 minutes by default, at most 480 — and never past the expiry of the credential that asks (a delegated token, or your signed-in session).

commitSha.description: The full id of the commit to build. Without it, the commit of the project’s newest recorded validation — which need not be `main`’s head: name the commit you mean.

StreamFrame.description: Every message on WS /v1/projects/{projectId}/events is one of these, as JSON. Switch on `kind`, then `type`.

SubmitLaunchRecordRequest.description: That a request to UBC was sent: the day, its reference if there is one, and which draft was sent.

sentAt.description: The day it was sent, `YYYY-MM-DD` — today or earlier, and not before the draft was made. Today in Vancouver when absent.

reference.description: UBC’s reference for the request, when you have one yet.

draftGeneratedAt.description: The `generatedAt` of the draft you sent, as you read it. If it has been drafted again since, the request is refused `409 LAUNCH_DRAFT_CHANGED` rather than recording a draft you never saw. Send it whenever you show a person the draft they send.

Token.description: A delegated token, scoped to one project and a capability set. Its secret is shown once, when it is minted, and is never readable again.

id.description: The token — what `revokeToken` names, and the `<id>` in its secret.

projectId.description: The one project it may act on.

name.description: The label its minter gave it.

capabilities.description: What it may do on that project; nothing else.

rateLimit.description: Requests a minute this token may make, enforced in the control plane. Past it, every route answers 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After.

expired.description: Whether this token is past its own expiresAt. Computed by the platform; a revoked token that has not expired is not expired.

revokedAt.description: When a person revoked it; null while it is not revoked. A revoked token is refused `UNAUTHENTICATED`.

lastUsedAt.description: When it last authenticated a request; null if never.

TokenList.description: The project’s delegated tokens — revoked and expired ones included.

UpdateProjectRequest.description: What to change about a project. Only its name can change; its slug never does.

name.description: What people call the project — text of 1 to 80 characters, trimmed, on one line, with something visible in it; no control character, line separator or bidirectional mark. Never part of an address: the slug is.

id.description: Their user id.

displayName.description: Their name, as CWL gave it.

ValidateSpecRequest.description: Which commit’s manifest.yaml to validate; `{}` validates `main`’s head.

x-manifest-unversioned.why: Browser-mediated sign-in. Its URL is part of the flow the Manifest IdP completes, not a resource.

Step-up re-authentication: a second sign-in, for the actions that ask for one. A browser navigation that ends at the IdP and returns through the ACS; it re-proves a person rather than naming a resource, and its answer is a redirect rather than a representation.
The ACS. Its URL is registered with the IdP in the platform's SP row, so a prefix change would be an IdP registration change.
The console's own sign-out. Ends Manifest's session and answers where the browser goes next — the IdP's single logout, so the IdP's session ends too; not a resource.
The SLO URL registered beside the ACS, reached by the IdP's HTTP-Redirect binding, which is a GET: the IdP's signed LogoutRequest, or its signed LogoutResponse to a console sign-out.
The registry token realm. Its callers are the Docker daemon and BuildKit speaking the distribution token protocol, never a Manifest client.
The registry token realm, OAuth2 form grant. Same callers, same reason.

GitHub's deliveries, for a control plane that runs the GitHub source driver: its caller is GitHub, never a Manifest client, and its credential is the delivery's HMAC signature rather than a session or a token. Reached at 127.0.0.1:7100 directly, as the edge itself reaches the control plane — never through the edge, which forwards only /v1/* and /auth/*. On the local source driver it answers every delivery 404 WEBHOOKS_NOT_CONFIGURED.

AGENT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.summary: The monthly agent budget of the person this credential acts for is spent, so no key was issued.
AGENT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.remedy: Wait for the month to reset (`getAgentBudget` says when), or ask a platform administrator to raise this person’s agent budget.

AGENT_NO_MODEL_FOR_CLASSIFICATION.summary: No model in the platform’s catalogue is approved for this project’s data classification, so no key was issued. An empty model list would be every model to the gateway.
AGENT_NO_MODEL_FOR_CLASSIFICATION.remedy: Ask a platform administrator to approve a model for this classification in the catalogue. The classification is the newest valid manifest’s, and never less restrictive than production’s release.

AGENT_SESSION_ALREADY_STARTED.summary: This request — its Idempotency-Key — already started an agent session, and its key was answered then. A key is shown once and never again.
AGENT_SESSION_ALREADY_STARTED.remedy: Use the key from the first answer. If it was lost, end the session this refusal names (`endAgentSession`) and start another with a new Idempotency-Key.

AI_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE.summary: The gateway could not be reached.
AI_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE.remedy: Retry later: the AI gateway did not answer.

AI_CATALOGUE_DISABLED.summary: AI is switched off on this control plane.
AI_CATALOGUE_DISABLED.remedy: Ask an administrator to switch AI on. A build or release can go on without AI: remove `ai.models` from manifest.yaml. A member removal or a token revocation answered this has already happened: repeat it once AI is back on, to end the agent sessions it left.

AI_CATALOGUE_EMPTY.summary: The gateway returned an empty model catalogue.
AI_CATALOGUE_EMPTY.remedy: Retry later, or ask an administrator: the AI gateway lists no models, so none can be declared or checked.

AI_KEY_EXPIRED.remedy: Deploy the app again: a deploy issues its instance a new key.

AI_KEY_REVOKED.remedy: Deploy the app again: a deploy issues its instance a new key.

AI_MODEL_NOT_PERMITTED.summary: The app’s key does not reach the model it asked for.
AI_MODEL_NOT_PERMITTED.remedy: Declare the model in manifest.yaml’s `ai.models`, then build, release and deploy: an app’s key reaches only the models its release declares.

AI_MODEL_UNKNOWN.summary: The gateway does not know the model.
AI_MODEL_UNKNOWN.remedy: Use a logical model name from the catalogue, never a vendor’s model id.

AI_PROJECT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.summary: The app has used its AI budget for the month.
AI_PROJECT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.remedy: Wait for next month’s budget, or raise `ai.budget.project_monthly_usd` within the project’s AI quota and release again.

AI_ROUTE_NOT_PERMITTED.summary: The app’s key does not reach that gateway route.
AI_ROUTE_NOT_PERMITTED.remedy: Call the gateway only through the routes the blueprint’s AI client uses; the key reaches no others.

AI_UNMAPPED.summary: The gateway answered with a failure this platform does not map.
AI_UNMAPPED.remedy: Retry once; if it recurs, report the time to the platform’s operator, whose log has the gateway’s answer.

AI_USER_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.summary: The person has used their AI allowance for the month.
AI_USER_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.remedy: Wait for next month’s allowance, or ask an administrator to raise it.

APPROVAL_NOT_NEEDED.summary: The release serving staging needs no administrator’s approval: one already covers it, or — for an app that has launched — it changes nothing that needs one. The message says which. Nothing was asked.
APPROVAL_NOT_NEEDED.remedy: Nothing to ask for: read the launch checklist (`getLaunchReadiness`) for what is still unmet, and deploy to production once it is ready.

APPROVAL_PREVIEW_EXPIRED.summary: The preview is older than thirty minutes, so it is no longer what was shown at decision time; take a new one.
APPROVAL_PREVIEW_EXPIRED.remedy: Take a new preview (`createApprovalPreview`), read it, and decide naming the new one.

APPROVAL_PREVIEW_REQUIRED.summary: An approval or rejection names no preview. Take one (`POST /v1/releases/{releaseId}/approval-preview`), read it, and decide naming its id.
APPROVAL_PREVIEW_REQUIRED.remedy: Take a preview (`createApprovalPreview`), read it, and send the decision again naming its `previewId`.

APPROVAL_PREVIEW_STALE.summary: What the release would be approved as changed since the preview was taken — in practice another decision moved the last approved release. Take a new preview and read it.
APPROVAL_PREVIEW_STALE.remedy: Take a new preview (`createApprovalPreview`), read what changed, and decide naming the new one.

BLUEPRINT_NOT_FOUND.summary: No blueprint with this reference is in the registry.
BLUEPRINT_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Choose one from `listBlueprints` and name it `name@major`.

BUILDING_NOT_OPEN.summary: Building on Manifest — creating a project or starting an intake session — is open only to faculty members and platform administrators for now, and the signed-in person is neither. Nothing was created.
BUILDING_NOT_OPEN.remedy: Read `mayBuild` on `getMe` before offering to build, and tell a person for whom it is false that building is not open to them yet. The affiliation is read at sign-in, so a faculty member refused should sign out and sign in again first; if they still may not build, a platform administrator can help.

CONFIG_BUILD_CREDENTIAL_SECRET_REQUIRED.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_CONTROL_PLANE_ORIGIN_PORT_MISMATC.summary: A loopback origin names a port the control plane does not listen on.
CONFIG_CONTROL_PLANE_ORIGIN_PORT_MISMATC.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_FRONTEND_ORIGIN_PORT_MISMATCH.summary: MANIFEST_FRONTEND_ORIGIN is a loopback origin naming a port the control plane does not listen on.
CONFIG_FRONTEND_ORIGIN_PORT_MISMATCH.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_GITHUB_FAKE_OUTSIDE_DEVELOPMENT.summary: A GitHub URL names loopback — the fake GitHub a laptop runs — on the GitHub driver outside development.
CONFIG_GITHUB_FAKE_OUTSIDE_DEVELOPMENT.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_GITHUB_INSECURE_URL.summary: A GitHub URL is plain http beyond loopback, so an installation token would cross the network in plaintext.
CONFIG_GITHUB_INSECURE_URL.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_INVALID.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY_REQUIRED.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_MASTER_SECRET_REQUIRED.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CONFIG_ORIGINS_SHARE_A_HOST.summary: MANIFEST_CONTROL_PLANE_ORIGIN and MANIFEST_FRONTEND_ORIGIN are on one host, so a request could not say which it arrived on.
CONFIG_ORIGINS_SHARE_A_HOST.remedy: The control plane refuses to start until its operator corrects the setting the message names; nothing a client sends changes it.

CREDENTIAL_AMBIGUOUS.summary: The request carried both a session cookie and a delegated token; it carries one or the other.
CREDENTIAL_AMBIGUOUS.remedy: Send one credential: the session cookie from a browser, or `Authorization: Bearer` from a program — never both.

CSRF_ORIGIN_REFUSED.summary: A request carrying a session did not come from the origin it was sent to. Each of Manifest’s origins — the console’s, and the faculty front-end’s — takes a session’s request only from itself.
CSRF_ORIGIN_REFUSED.remedy: Send `Origin` naming the origin the request is sent to — a browser does this itself, and `hint` names it. A session is its own origin’s: one set on the other origin is not a session here. A program that is not a browser sends a delegated token rather than a session cookie; a token needs no Origin.

DOC_NOT_FOUND.summary: No page of the API’s documentation has this slug.
DOC_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Read the index (`listDocs`): it names every page with the slug to read it by. A page’s links name files — `authoring.md` is the slug `authoring`, `reference/errors.md` is `reference-errors`.

EVENTS_UPGRADE_REQUIRED.summary: The event stream is a WebSocket; a plain GET cannot read it.
EVENTS_UPGRADE_REQUIRED.remedy: Open the same URL as a WebSocket (`wss://`), with the same credential.

FORBIDDEN.summary: A member of the project whose role does not hold this capability.
FORBIDDEN.remedy: Ask one of the project’s owners (`listMembers` names them) for a role that holds this capability — or, for a token, mint one that holds it (`mintToken`).

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.summary: A mutation arrived without an Idempotency-Key of at least 8 characters.
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.remedy: Send `Idempotency-Key` with every mutation: a new random value of 8 characters or more — a UUID — for each user action, reused unchanged when retrying that same action.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.summary: This Idempotency-Key was used on this route for a different request — another resource in the path, or a different body.
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.remedy: Use a new Idempotency-Key for a new action. To retry the SAME action, send the same key to the same path with exactly the same body, and the first answer is replayed — except a mint, whose secret is never kept (`TOKEN_ALREADY_MINTED`).

INCIDENT_LOG_CONFIDENTIAL.summary: A confidential project’s staging and production Incidents are not answered to a delegated token while the platform lets that project’s building agent use the capable model: their log tails can carry the input of the real people the classification protects, and redaction does not remove names or student numbers.
INCIDENT_LOG_CONFIDENTIAL.remedy: Read the sandbox’s Incidents instead — its users are test users — or ask the person you work for to read this environment’s Incidents in their own session and tell you, in their own words, what failed — never to paste its log tail or prompt to you, which is what this protects.

INSTANCE_OUTPUT_PRODUCTION.summary: A production instance’s output is not readable: it serves real people, whose input its output can carry.
INSTANCE_OUTPUT_PRODUCTION.remedy: Read a sandbox instance’s output instead, or a failed production instance’s Incident (`listIncidents`) — its log tail is the only window onto production.

INSTANCE_OUTPUT_STAGING.summary: A staging instance’s output is not readable: staging serves real people — staging CWL holders at UBC — whose input its output can carry. Decided by the environment’s kind, so a laptop’s staging is refused too.
INSTANCE_OUTPUT_STAGING.remedy: Read a sandbox instance’s output instead — deploy the same release there (`deploy`) to see what it prints — or a failed staging instance’s Incident (`listIncidents`), whose log tail is the only window onto staging.

INSTANCE_OUTPUT_UNAVAILABLE.summary: The instance no longer runs, or never started, so there is no output to read — Manifest keeps none.
INSTANCE_OUTPUT_UNAVAILABLE.remedy: Read the environment’s Incidents (`listIncidents`): a failed instance’s last lines are in its Incident. `listInstances` says which instance is running now.

INTAKE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.summary: The platform’s monthly intake budget is spent, so describing new apps is paused for everyone until the month resets. It is never charged to a person’s budget instead.
INTAKE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.remedy: Wait for the month to reset — the first of the month, 00:00 UTC — or ask a platform administrator to raise the intake budget.

INTAKE_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED.summary: This person has started the intake sessions a person may start in a day, so describing new apps is paused for them until midnight, Vancouver time.
INTAKE_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED.remedy: Try again tomorrow, or create the project now and continue under an agent session (`startAgentSession`), which is charged to the person instead.

INTAKE_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE.summary: The platform’s intake model is not a catalogue model approved for internal data, so intake is paused rather than sent to another model.
INTAKE_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE.remedy: A platform administrator names an intake model the catalogue approves for internal data (`MANIFEST_INTAKE_MODEL`).

INTAKE_SESSION_ALREADY_STARTED.summary: This request — its Idempotency-Key — already started an intake session, and its key was answered then. A key is shown once and never again.
INTAKE_SESSION_ALREADY_STARTED.remedy: Use the key from the first answer. If it was lost, end the session this refusal names (`endIntakeSession`) and start another with a new Idempotency-Key.

INTERNAL.summary: The control plane failed; its operator log has the reason. Nothing the client sent explains it.
INTERNAL.remedy: Retry once; if it recurs, the platform’s operator has a line naming it — report the time and the operation.

LAUNCH_DRAFT_CHANGED.summary: The draft was made again after the one the request names (`draftGeneratedAt`), so what Manifest holds is not what was sent. Nothing was recorded.
LAUNCH_DRAFT_CHANGED.remedy: Read the current draft (`getLaunchRecords`). If it is what you sent, say so again with its `generatedAt`; if you sent the earlier one, send the current draft instead and say so.

LAUNCH_DRAFT_REQUIRED.summary: There is no draft of this registration or privacy assessment to have sent: Manifest drafts it, and what a person sends is that draft.
LAUNCH_DRAFT_REQUIRED.remedy: Draft it first (`draftIamRegistration` for a registration, `draftPrivacyAssessment` for the privacy assessment), send the draft to UBC, then say it was sent. Nothing was recorded.

LAUNCH_DRAFT_STALE.summary: The registration’s draft does not carry the privacy assessment’s PIA number, which UBC IAM asks for: it was drafted before the assessment was approved with it, or the number has changed since. Nothing was recorded.
LAUNCH_DRAFT_STALE.remedy: Draft the registration again (`draftIamRegistration`) — the new draft carries the PIA number — send that one, then say it was sent.

LAUNCH_NOT_CWL.summary: The app signs nobody in with CWL — or asks for no attribute, which no registration may — so there is nothing to register with UBC IAM.
LAUNCH_NOT_CWL.remedy: An app that signs nobody in needs no registration. To sign people in, set `auth.provider: cwl` and the attributes the app needs in `auth.attributes`, validate the manifest, then draft again.

LAUNCH_PIA_NOT_APPROVED.summary: Neither registration is sent until the privacy assessment is approved and carries its reference, the PIA number UBC IAM asks for. UBC’s order is the assessment first.
LAUNCH_PIA_NOT_APPROVED.remedy: Send the privacy assessment first. Once an administrator records it approved, with its PIA number, send the registration and say so again.

LAUNCH_RECORD_INVALID.summary: An external record’s fields cannot be accepted — for example an empty registered-attribute list, against which every release’s attributes would pass the check that they are registered; the message names the field.
LAUNCH_RECORD_INVALID.remedy: Correct the fields the message names — a registration lists at least one attribute — and record it again.

LAUNCH_RECORD_SUBMITTED.summary: This record has been sent, and what was sent is kept as it was sent. A registration that is with UBC IAM or registered by it (`submitted` or `active`) is drafted again only once UBC asks for changes or the registration lapses; a privacy assessment that is with the Privacy Office or approved by it (`submitted` or `approved`), only once the Office sends it back.
LAUNCH_RECORD_SUBMITTED.remedy: To change what was sent, ask UBC IAM or the Privacy Office. Once an administrator records that UBC asked for changes (`change_requested`), that the registration lapsed (`expired`), or that the assessment came back (`draft`), draft it again.

LAUNCH_SENT_AT_INVALID.summary: The day given for when it was sent cannot be true: it is after today in Vancouver, or before the draft that was sent was made.
LAUNCH_SENT_AT_INVALID.remedy: Give the day you sent it, as YYYY-MM-DD — today or earlier, and not before the draft’s day — or leave it out for today.

LAUNCH_STAGING_NOT_REGISTERED.summary: The production registration is sent only once the staging registration is active — registered by UBC IAM, and the app tested at staging. UBC’s order is staging before production.
LAUNCH_STAGING_NOT_REGISTERED.remedy: Send the staging registration first. Once an administrator records it active and you have tested the app at staging, send the production registration and say so again.

LAUNCH_TRANSITION_INVALID.summary: An IAM registration or a privacy assessment was asked to move to a state it cannot reach from the one it is in; the message names what that state CAN become.
LAUNCH_TRANSITION_INVALID.remedy: Move the record through its states one step at a time, to one of the states the message names.

MEMBER_MAY_NOT_BUILD.summary: The person named may not build on Manifest — only faculty members and platform administrators may, for now — so they cannot be added to a project. The message names them; nobody was added.
MEMBER_MAY_NOT_BUILD.remedy: Add a faculty colleague instead. A person already on the project keeps their place, and their role can still be changed.

MEMBER_USER_AMBIGUOUS.summary: More than one person who has signed in to Manifest has the email given, so it names nobody in particular. The answer names none of them.
MEMBER_USER_AMBIGUOUS.remedy: Add the person by their CWL login name (`cwlLogin`) or their PUID (`puid`) instead.

MEMBER_USER_NOT_FOUND.summary: Nobody Manifest knows by the PUID, CWL login name or email given has signed in. A CWL login name is known only for a person who has signed in since Manifest began asking CWL for one, so a person who has signed in can still miss by login.
MEMBER_USER_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check it. For a CWL login name, add the person by their email or PUID instead; otherwise ask them to sign in to Manifest once with CWL, then add them again.

NOT_FOUND.summary: No such resource — or one the caller has no business knowing exists.
NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check the id. If it is right you cannot see it: ask one of the project’s owners to add you (`addMember`), or use a token minted for that project.

PENDING_ACTION_RESOLVED.summary: This pending action has already been confirmed or rejected; it cannot be answered twice.
PENDING_ACTION_RESOLVED.remedy: Read it again (`getPendingAction`): somebody has already answered, and its `state` says how.

PROJECT_ARCHIVED.summary: The project is archived — switched off by its owner — so it can be read and restored, and nothing else can change.
PROJECT_ARCHIVED.remedy: Restore it (`restoreProject`, the owner or an administrator, in their own session), then deploy to bring it back. A delegated token of an archived project was revoked with it: mint a new one after the restore.

PROJECT_LAST_OWNER.summary: A project must always have an owner, so the last one cannot be removed or made a collaborator.
PROJECT_LAST_OWNER.remedy: Make another member an owner first (`addMember` with role `owner`), then remove this one or change their role.

PROJECT_LAUNCHED_NOT_DELETABLE.summary: The project has been to production, so it cannot be deleted: its data is disposed of under its retention period and UBC’s sunset procedure, which are the Privacy Office’s, and its production name stays held for good. Nothing was destroyed — and nothing was changed, unless the launch completed while the delete was starting, when the app has been switched off (archived) with everything kept.
PROJECT_LAUNCHED_NOT_DELETABLE.remedy: Archive it instead (`archiveProject`) to switch it off for everyone; its data and records are kept for their retention period. One the delete switched off is restored with `restoreProject`.

PROJECT_TEARDOWN_INCOMPLETE.summary: Switching the project off, or deleting it, stopped at a step (named in the message). It is archived — nothing new starts — but something it ran, or something a delete destroys, may still be there.
PROJECT_TEARDOWN_INCOMPLETE.remedy: Send the same request again: every finished step answers at once, and the rest continue. The control plane’s next boot finishes an archive too — never a delete, which only the same request finishes. If it keeps stopping at the same step, tell a platform administrator.

RATE_LIMITED.summary: Too many requests from this credential; Retry-After says when to try again. A delegated token has a limit of its own, fixed when it was minted.
RATE_LIMITED.remedy: Wait the number of seconds `Retry-After` gives, then retry. A token’s limit is its `rateLimit`, fixed when it was minted.

REHEARSAL_DEPLOY_FAILED.summary: The candidate could not be deployed to production, or the deploy registered no Service Provider.
REHEARSAL_DEPLOY_FAILED.remedy: Read the message and the project’s events for why the deploy failed, fix that, and rehearse again.

REHEARSAL_LAUNCHED.summary: The app has launched, so a rehearsal would put an unapproved candidate on its live production listener. A registration change is proved by UBC IAM’s change request.
REHEARSAL_LAUNCHED.remedy: Nothing to rehearse: a launched app’s registration change goes to UBC IAM as a change request, which an administrator records (`recordIamRegistration`).

REHEARSAL_NOT_CWL.summary: The app signs nobody in with CWL, so it registers no Service Provider and there is nothing to rehearse. Its checklist item is met.
REHEARSAL_NOT_CWL.remedy: Nothing to do: the launch checklist’s rehearsal item is already met for an app with no CWL sign-in.

REHEARSAL_NO_CANDIDATE.summary: Nothing is serving staging, so there is no candidate release to rehearse.
REHEARSAL_NO_CANDIDATE.remedy: Deploy a release to staging and let it become healthy, then rehearse again.

REHEARSAL_RUNNING.summary: A rehearsal of this project is already running, so this one was not started and nothing was deployed.
REHEARSAL_RUNNING.remedy: Wait for the running rehearsal to answer — up to about two minutes — then read the launch checklist (`getLaunchReadiness`): its `rehearsal` item says how it went.

REHEARSAL_TEARDOWN_FAILED.summary: The rehearsal ran, but could not take its production instance down afterwards (the message says what is left), so its result was not recorded.
REHEARSAL_TEARDOWN_FAILED.remedy: Run the rehearsal again: it deploys the candidate afresh and takes it down again. If it keeps failing, tell a platform administrator: the control plane’s operator log names the step that failed.

RELEASE_AI_BUDGET_MISSING.summary: The release declares models and no AI budget.
RELEASE_AI_BUDGET_MISSING.remedy: Set `ai.budget.project_monthly_usd` above 0 in manifest.yaml, or ask an administrator to raise the project’s AI quota, then build and release again. A budget of 0 would refuse the app’s every question.

RELEASE_AI_DISABLED.summary: The release declares models and AI is switched off on this control plane.
RELEASE_AI_DISABLED.remedy: Remove `ai.models` from manifest.yaml and release again to deploy without AI, or ask an administrator to switch AI on.

RELEASE_BLUEPRINT_NOT_FOUND.summary: The project’s blueprint is no longer in the registry.
RELEASE_BLUEPRINT_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Ask an administrator to restore the blueprint to the registry; nothing in the project can change it.

RELEASE_BUILD_NOT_DEPLOYABLE.summary: The build did not succeed, so nothing can be released from it.
RELEASE_BUILD_NOT_DEPLOYABLE.remedy: Read the build’s log (`getBuildLog`), fix the cause, build again (`startBuild`) and release the build that succeeds.

RELEASE_BUILD_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check the build id; `listBuilds` lists the project’s builds.

RELEASE_DIGEST_MISSING.summary: The release’s build recorded no digest.
RELEASE_DIGEST_MISSING.remedy: Build the commit again (`startBuild`) and create the release from the new build (`createRelease`).

RELEASE_DIGEST_NOT_APPROVED.summary: This production deploy needs an administrator’s approval — a first launch, or a launched app’s change to a sensitive field — and none covers the digest it would run; or an administrator rejected this release, which is final. The message says which.
RELEASE_DIGEST_NOT_APPROVED.remedy: Ask an administrator to approve this release (`requestApproval`) — the request waits in their queue — then deploy again. A rejected release stays rejected: build and release a new one.

RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check the environment id; `listEnvironments` lists the project’s three.

RELEASE_IMAGE_REPOSITORY_MISSING.summary: The build recorded a digest and no repository; rebuild it.
RELEASE_IMAGE_REPOSITORY_MISSING.remedy: Build the commit again (`startBuild`) and create the release from the new build (`createRelease`).

RELEASE_LOCAL_IMAGE_ON_REMOTE_DRIVER.summary: A laptop-built image cannot reach a remote driver.
RELEASE_LOCAL_IMAGE_ON_REMOTE_DRIVER.remedy: Nothing a client can change: this control plane builds on one machine and runs on another. Report it to the platform’s operator.

RELEASE_MODEL_CLASSIFICATION_TOO_LOW.summary: A declared model is not approved for the app’s data classification.
RELEASE_MODEL_CLASSIFICATION_TOO_LOW.remedy: Declare a model approved for the app’s `data.classification`, or lower the classification if it is overstated; then build and release again.

RELEASE_MODEL_NOT_IN_CATALOGUE.summary: A declared model is no longer in the catalogue.
RELEASE_MODEL_NOT_IN_CATALOGUE.remedy: Declare a model the catalogue has — `validateSpec` names them when one is unknown — then build and release again.

RELEASE_MODEL_UNCLASSIFIED.summary: A declared model has no classification in the catalogue.
RELEASE_MODEL_UNCLASSIFIED.remedy: Declare another model, or ask an administrator to classify this one; then build and release again.

RELEASE_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check the release id; `listReleases` lists the project’s releases.

RELEASE_NOT_STAGED.summary: Only the release serving staging may go to production, or be asked about for sign-off — production runs exactly what staging ran; the body carries the LaunchReadiness of the one that is.
RELEASE_NOT_STAGED.remedy: Deploy this release to staging first and let it become healthy — or name the release serving staging (`candidateReleaseId` in the body): deploy that one to production, or ask for sign-off on it.

RELEASE_PRODUCTION_GATE_UNAVAILABLE.summary: A blocking item an approval alone cannot fix is unmet — on a first launch’s checklist, or a launched app’s, a rejected release included; the body carries LaunchReadiness.
RELEASE_PRODUCTION_GATE_UNAVAILABLE.remedy: Read `launchReadiness`: each unmet blocking item says what meets it. Meet them — most are records an administrator keeps, some with long lead times — and deploy again; a retry alone changes nothing.

RELEASE_PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.summary: The environment names a project that does not exist.
RELEASE_PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check the environment id: its project has been deleted, and nothing can be deployed to it.

RELEASE_REESCALATED.summary: A launched app’s release changes a sensitive field since the last approved release, and only an administrator’s approval is missing; the body carries LaunchReadiness.
RELEASE_REESCALATED.remedy: Ask an administrator to approve this release (`requestApproval`) — the request waits in their queue — then deploy again once they have.

RELEASE_REJECTED.summary: An administrator did not approve this release, and a rejection is final for the release it was made on; the message carries their reason. Nothing was asked.
RELEASE_REJECTED.remedy: Read the administrator’s reason (`getApproval`), change the app, build and release it, deploy that release to staging, and ask for sign-off on it.

RELEASE_SECRET_NOT_SET.summary: The release’s manifest.yaml declares a secret (`secret: true`) that has no value in this environment, so nothing was started. Set each name the message lists with `setAppSecret`, then deploy again.
RELEASE_SECRET_NOT_SET.remedy: Set each name the message lists in this environment (`setAppSecret`) and deploy again; `listAppSecrets` shows which are set.

REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE.summary: The request body is larger than the API accepts.
REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE.remedy: Send a smaller body. Every operation accepts at most 1 MiB except `createCommit`, which accepts 8 MiB — split a larger change into several commits.

REQUEST_INVALID.summary: A field in the request is missing or malformed, or the body could not be read at all; the message says which.
REQUEST_INVALID.remedy: Read `message`: it names each part and field that failed (`body.changes.0.path: …`). Correct them against this operation’s schema and send it again. A request with no body — a GET, or a DELETE that takes none — carries no `Content-Type`.

REQUEST_MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED.summary: The request body is a content type the route does not read.
REQUEST_MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED.remedy: Send the body as JSON, with `Content-Type: application/json`.

ROUTE_NOT_FOUND.summary: No route has this method and path. Resource routes are under /v1/.
ROUTE_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check the method and the path against this document: every resource route begins `/v1/`, and a path parameter is an id, never a name.

SAML_ASSERTION_REJECTED.summary: The assertion was refused; the operator log says why.
SAML_ASSERTION_REJECTED.remedy: Start the sign-in again at /auth/login. If it keeps failing, report the time to the platform’s operator, whose log has the reason.

SAML_LOGIN_NOT_BOUND.summary: The assertion answers a sign-in this browser did not start.
SAML_LOGIN_NOT_BOUND.remedy: Start the sign-in again at /auth/login, in the browser that will receive the answer.

SAML_LOGOUT_REJECTED.summary: The single-logout request could not be verified; the operator log says why.
SAML_LOGOUT_REJECTED.remedy: Nothing a client can change: this endpoint’s caller is the identity provider. The platform’s operator log says why its request could not be verified.

SAML_NO_PUID.remedy: Nothing the person can change: the identity provider’s registration for Manifest must release ubcEduCwlPuid. Report it to the platform’s operator.

SAML_STEP_UP_NO_SESSION.summary: The step-up came back to a browser holding no valid session; sign in again.
SAML_STEP_UP_NO_SESSION.remedy: Sign in again at /auth/login, then step up.

SAML_STEP_UP_WRONG_USER.summary: The step-up assertion is for a different person than the session in this browser.
SAML_STEP_UP_WRONG_USER.remedy: Step up as the person who is signed in — or sign out, sign in as the other person, and step up then.

SAML_USER_UPSERT_FAILED.summary: The user could not be recorded.
SAML_USER_UPSERT_FAILED.remedy: Start the sign-in again at /auth/login. If it keeps failing, report the time to the platform’s operator.

SECRET_NAME_RESERVED.summary: That variable is one the platform sets for every app — the platform’s value always wins — so it cannot be an app secret. Choose another name.
SECRET_NAME_RESERVED.remedy: Name the secret something else, in manifest.yaml and here. The platform’s own variables are listed in the blueprint’s knowledge pack (`getKnowledgePack`).

SLUG_INVALID.summary: The slug breaks the rule for slugs.
SLUG_INVALID.remedy: Choose a slug of 3 to 39 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens that starts with a letter. `checkSlug` checks one without creating anything.

SLUG_RESERVED.summary: The slug is a reserved label — a slug no project may take; the message says what it stands for.
SLUG_RESERVED.remedy: Choose another slug. `checkSlug` says whether one is free.

SLUG_TAKEN.remedy: Choose another slug. `checkSlug` says whether one is free.

SOURCE_COMMIT_NOT_FOUND.summary: The repository has no such commit — or what was named is not a full commit id — so there is nothing to build or read from it.
SOURCE_COMMIT_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Name the full 40-character id of a commit the repository has; `listCommits` lists them.

SOURCE_CONFLICT.summary: The branch moved after the commit this request was computed from; read it again and retry.
SOURCE_CONFLICT.remedy: Read the tree again (`getTree`) for its `commitSha`, recompute your changes against it, and commit with that as `baseCommit`.

SOURCE_FILE_NOT_TEXT.summary: The file is binary or not UTF-8, so it is not read as text.
SOURCE_FILE_NOT_TEXT.remedy: Read it as bytes: `getFile` with `encoding=base64` answers any file up to 2 MiB. `getTree` marks a binary file `binary: true`.

SOURCE_FILE_TOO_LARGE.summary: The file is larger than the API carries in one read — 1 MiB as text, 2 MiB with `encoding=base64`.
SOURCE_FILE_TOO_LARGE.remedy: A text file between 1 and 2 MiB can be READ with `encoding=base64`, and changed only with git directly, by a push — as can any file past 2 MiB. `getTree` gives every file’s `size`.

SOURCE_GITHUB_KEY_UNREADABLE.summary: The GitHub App’s private key cannot be read, or is not an RSA key; the message names the file.
SOURCE_GITHUB_KEY_UNREADABLE.remedy: Nothing a client can change: the platform’s operator restores the key file, readable by its owner alone.

SOURCE_GITHUB_REFUSED.summary: GitHub refused the request; the message carries GitHub’s own message and nothing else of its answer.
SOURCE_GITHUB_REFUSED.remedy: Read GitHub’s message: a limit passes with time, and a permission is the GitHub App installation’s to grant. Retry once it is resolved.

SOURCE_GIT_FAILED.summary: git failed; the message names the operation.
SOURCE_GIT_FAILED.remedy: Retry once; if it recurs, report the time and the operation the message names to the platform’s operator.

SOURCE_INVALID_SLUG.summary: The slug cannot name a repository.
SOURCE_INVALID_SLUG.remedy: Choose a slug of 3 to 39 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens that starts with a letter; `checkSlug` checks one.

SOURCE_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT.summary: Every change leaves its file as it is in the base commit, so there is nothing to commit.
SOURCE_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT.remedy: Nothing to do: every file already reads as you would write it. Read the file again (`getFile`) if you expected a difference.

SOURCE_PATH_CONFLICT.summary: A change does not fit the base commit’s tree: a file where a directory is, a path under a file, a symlink or a submodule, something other than a regular file to overwrite or a file to delete, or one path named twice; the message names the path.
SOURCE_PATH_CONFLICT.remedy: Read the tree at `baseCommit` (`getTree`) and change the path the message names: write beside a directory rather than over it, delete a directory’s files one by one, and name each path once. A symlink or a submodule is changed with git directly.

SOURCE_PATH_ESCAPE.summary: A slug that would leave the repository root, or a path that is not inside the repository — absolute, or with an empty, `.` or `..` component — or into a repository’s own `.git`.
SOURCE_PATH_ESCAPE.remedy: Name a path relative to the repository root, `/`-separated, with no empty, `.`, `..` or `.git` component.

SOURCE_PATH_NOT_A_FILE.summary: The path names a directory, a symlink or a submodule; the API reads and writes regular files.
SOURCE_PATH_NOT_A_FILE.remedy: Name a file; `getTree` says what each path is, and lists a directory’s contents.

SOURCE_PATH_NOT_FOUND.summary: The commit has no such path — so there is nothing to read, or to delete.
SOURCE_PATH_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Check the path against `getTree` at the same commit; paths are case-sensitive.

SOURCE_PROVIDER_MISMATCH.summary: The project’s repository was not made by the source driver this control plane runs: either a different driver made it (driver 1’s local repository, or driver 2’s GitHub one), or the same GitHub driver made it against another GitHub — the fake or the real App, told apart by the API host recorded when the repository was made (one recorded before Manifest kept that host is answered by whichever GitHub is running); the message names both the driver or host that made it and the one running.
SOURCE_PROVIDER_MISMATCH.remedy: Use a control plane running the project’s own driver, and for driver 2 the same GitHub (`MANIFEST_GITHUB_API_URL`): a project stays with the driver, and the GitHub, that created its repository.

SOURCE_REF_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Name `main`, another branch the repository has, or a full 40-character commit id.

SOURCE_REPOSITORY_EXISTS.summary: A repository of that name already exists — on GitHub, or as a mirror on this machine — and Manifest never adopts one it did not create.
SOURCE_REPOSITORY_EXISTS.remedy: Choose another slug. A leftover repository of that name is removed by whoever owns it; Manifest will not take it over.

SOURCE_REPOSITORY_NOT_PRIVATE.summary: GitHub did not create the repository private, so it was deleted.
SOURCE_REPOSITORY_NOT_PRIVATE.remedy: Create the project again. If it recurs, the GitHub organisation’s settings forbid private repositories, and its administrator changes them.

SOURCE_REPOSITORY_PUBLIC.summary: The repository was last read PUBLIC on GitHub and could not be made private; it is not built while it is public.
SOURCE_REPOSITORY_PUBLIC.remedy: Make the repository private on GitHub. The next push or read checks it again, and building resumes.

SOURCE_SECRET_DETECTED.summary: A commit Manifest was asked to make carries a secret-shaped value, and nothing was committed; the message names path:line and the rule, never the value.
SOURCE_SECRET_DETECTED.remedy: Remove the value from the file — or the commit message — the message names, and never commit a credential: set it as an app secret instead (`setAppSecret`) and read it from the environment. Then commit again. In a file written with `encoding: base64`, the line counts runs of printable text, not lines.

SOURCE_UNREACHABLE.summary: The git host did not answer. A commit already mirrored still builds.
SOURCE_UNREACHABLE.remedy: Retry when the git host answers. Meanwhile a commit already mirrored still builds, releases and deploys.

SPEC_INVALID.summary: manifest.yaml at this commit is not valid; `details` lists each error with its path.
SPEC_INVALID.remedy: Read `details`: each entry names a path in manifest.yaml, a code (`ManifestErrorCode`), a message and usually a hint. Correct each one and commit the file again (`createCommit`); `validateSpec` checks it without building.

SPEC_NOT_FOUND.summary: The project has no validated spec yet.
SPEC_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Validate the manifest on `main` (`validateSpec`), or commit one (`createCommit`), and try again.

STARTER_NOT_FOUND.summary: The blueprint offers no starter by that name.
STARTER_NOT_FOUND.remedy: Choose one of the starters `getBlueprint` lists, or leave `starter` out for the skeleton alone.

STEP_UP_REQUIRED.summary: This action needs a second authentication round trip. Send the person to /auth/step-up and retry.
STEP_UP_REQUIRED.remedy: Send the person’s browser to `/auth/step-up?returnTo=<the page they are on>`, let them complete the CWL prompt, and repeat the request within ten minutes. A token cannot step up.

TOKEN_ACTION_PENDING.summary: A delegated token asked for one of the four privileged actions (`release:promote`, `secret:read`, `quota:set`, `members:manage`); `pendingAction` is the question a person must answer.
TOKEN_ACTION_PENDING.remedy: Ask the person who minted the token to confirm `pendingAction` in the console, then retry the identical request — same body, same Idempotency-Key — once. The confirmation grants exactly one retry.

TOKEN_ACTION_REJECTED.summary: A person refused this exact request. `pendingAction.reason` is why, in their words; retrying it will not change the answer.
TOKEN_ACTION_REJECTED.remedy: Do not retry it. Read `pendingAction.reason`, then ask the person, or ask for something different.

TOKEN_ALREADY_MINTED.summary: A mint was retried with its Idempotency-Key: the first request minted the token named, and its secret was shown to that request alone and is not kept.
TOKEN_ALREADY_MINTED.remedy: If you have the first answer’s secret, use it. If that answer was lost, revoke the token named (`revokeToken`) and mint again with a new Idempotency-Key.

TOKEN_CAPABILITY_FORBIDDEN.summary: A mint asked for one of the four privileged capabilities (`release:promote`, `secret:read`, `quota:set`, `members:manage`), or for a person-only one; the message names which.
TOKEN_CAPABILITY_FORBIDDEN.remedy: Mint the token without them. A privileged action is granted to a token one request at a time, by a person’s confirmation (`TOKEN_ACTION_PENDING`); a person-only one never is.

TOKEN_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED.summary: A valid delegated token asked for something only a person’s own interactive session may do.
TOKEN_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED.remedy: Have a person do it in the console, in their own session: no delegated token may, and no confirmation changes that. The operation’s description says when a token is refused.

TOKEN_PERSON_ONLY.summary: A delegated token asked for a person-only action — approving a release, recording UBC’s IAM or privacy decision, saying a request to UBC IAM or the Privacy Office was sent, running the pre-production rehearsal, or switching an app off, bringing it back or deleting it. Refused outright; no pending action is created.
TOKEN_PERSON_ONLY.remedy: A person does this, in the console, in their own session. No token can hold it and no confirmation grants it — do not ask for one.

UNAUTHENTICATED.summary: The request carries no valid credential — no session, or a delegated token that is unknown, revoked or expired.
UNAUTHENTICATED.remedy: Sign in at /auth/login for a session, or send a delegated token as `Authorization: Bearer mft_…`. A token that expired or was revoked is refused the same way: mint a new one (`mintToken`).

WEBHOOKS_NOT_CONFIGURED.summary: This control plane runs the local source driver, which receives no webhooks.
WEBHOOKS_NOT_CONFIGURED.remedy: Nothing to fix here: on the local driver a person pushes into Manifest’s own repository and no webhook is needed. Point a GitHub webhook only at a control plane that runs the GitHub driver.

WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD_INVALID.summary: A correctly signed delivery whose body is not a JSON object, or which lacks X-GitHub-Delivery or X-GitHub-Event.
WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD_INVALID.remedy: Send GitHub’s delivery unchanged: a JSON object, with its X-GitHub-Delivery and X-GitHub-Event headers.

WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID.summary: X-Hub-Signature-256 is well formed and does not match the body under the App’s webhook secret.
WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID.remedy: Make the App’s webhook secret and the control plane’s the same, and sign the exact bytes sent — a body re-serialised after signing no longer matches.

WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_MALFORMED.summary: X-Hub-Signature-256 is not exactly one sha256= and 64 lowercase hex characters.
WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_MALFORMED.remedy: Send the signature exactly as GitHub computes it: `sha256=` and the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, as 64 lowercase hex characters.

WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_MISSING.summary: The delivery carries no X-Hub-Signature-256 — including one that carries only the legacy SHA-1 X-Hub-Signature.
WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_MISSING.remedy: Give the GitHub App’s webhook its secret, so that GitHub signs every delivery with X-Hub-Signature-256. Only GitHub calls this endpoint; a Manifest client never does.

BLUEPRINT_AI_UNSUPPORTED.summary: The pinned blueprint does not provide AI.
BLUEPRINT_AI_UNSUPPORTED.remedy: Remove `ai.models`: an app gets AI only from a blueprint that provides it.

BLUEPRINT_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED.summary: The pinned blueprint does not support that `auth.provider`.
BLUEPRINT_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED.remedy: Set `auth.provider` to one the hint lists, which the pinned blueprint supports.

BLUEPRINT_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED.summary: The pinned blueprint does not understand this `manifest:` schema version.
BLUEPRINT_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED.remedy: Set `manifest:` to a schema version the hint lists.

BLUEPRINT_SERVICE_UNSUPPORTED.summary: The pinned blueprint cannot bind that service type.
BLUEPRINT_SERVICE_UNSUPPORTED.remedy: Use a service type the hint lists, which the pinned blueprint can bind.

SPEC_AI_BUDGET_REQUIRED.summary: The manifest declares a model and its AI budget is $0, which would refuse every request the app makes.
SPEC_AI_BUDGET_REQUIRED.remedy: Set `ai.budget.project_monthly_usd` above 0, or leave it out to use the project’s AI quota — and if that quota is $0, ask an administrator to raise it.

SPEC_AI_DISABLED.summary: The manifest declares models, and this platform offers none.
SPEC_AI_DISABLED.remedy: Remove `ai.models`, or ask an administrator to switch AI on.

SPEC_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_REGISTERED.summary: A launched app asks for a CWL attribute its recorded IAM registration does not release; refused when the production build runs.
SPEC_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_REGISTERED.remedy: Remove the attribute from `auth.attributes`, or have UBC IAM approve the registration’s change and record it (`recordIamRegistration`), then build again.

SPEC_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_WHITELISTED.summary: A CWL attribute UBC does not release to applications.
SPEC_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_WHITELISTED.remedy: Use an attribute the hint lists. The person’s identifier is `ubcEduCwlPuid`, never `uid`.

SPEC_BLUEPRINT_NOT_PINNED.summary: `blueprint` names a different blueprint from the one the project is pinned to; a commit cannot move a project.
SPEC_BLUEPRINT_NOT_PINNED.remedy: Set `blueprint` to the project’s pin, which the hint names.

SPEC_BUILD_BLOCK_FORBIDDEN.summary: manifest.yaml supplies its own build definition (`runtime.build`); the Dockerfile is the blueprint’s.
SPEC_BUILD_BLOCK_FORBIDDEN.remedy: Remove `runtime.build`. Declare what the app needs — never how to build it.

SPEC_ENV_NAME_RESERVED.summary: An `env` entry declares a variable the platform sets for every app.
SPEC_ENV_NAME_RESERVED.remedy: Remove the entry, or choose another name: the platform’s value always wins, so this line would do nothing.

SPEC_FIELD_NOT_ENFORCED.summary: A WARNING, not an error: a field Manifest validates and records with the release but does not enforce yet — today `ai.budget.per_user_monthly_usd`. The manifest is valid.
SPEC_FIELD_NOT_ENFORCED.remedy: Nothing to fix. Keep the value if you mean it — it applies once Manifest enforces it; what limits the app today is `ai.budget.project_monthly_usd`.

SPEC_INVALID_BLUEPRINT_REF.summary: `blueprint` is not a name pinned to a major version.
SPEC_INVALID_BLUEPRINT_REF.remedy: Write it as `name@major` — the project’s own pin, which `getProject` answers as `blueprint`.

SPEC_INVALID_SLUG.summary: `name` is not a valid project slug.
SPEC_INVALID_SLUG.remedy: Set `name` to the project’s slug: 3 to 39 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

SPEC_INVALID_VALUE.summary: A value has the wrong type, or is outside what its field permits.
SPEC_INVALID_VALUE.remedy: Correct the value the path names. This document’s `ManifestYaml` schema gives every field’s type and permitted values.

SPEC_MODEL_CLASSIFICATION_TOO_LOW.summary: A model that is not approved for the app’s `data.classification`.
SPEC_MODEL_CLASSIFICATION_TOO_LOW.remedy: Choose a model approved for that classification, or lower `data.classification` if it is overstated.

SPEC_MODEL_UNCLASSIFIED.summary: A model with no data classification, which no app may use.
SPEC_MODEL_UNCLASSIFIED.remedy: Choose another model, or ask an administrator to classify this one.

SPEC_MODEL_UNKNOWN.summary: A model the catalogue does not name.
SPEC_MODEL_UNKNOWN.remedy: Use a logical model name the hint lists, never a vendor’s model id.

SPEC_NAME_SLUG_MISMATCH.remedy: Set `name` to the project’s slug, which `getProject` answers as `slug`.

SPEC_PATH_EXPECTED.summary: A field that takes a path was given a URL.
SPEC_PATH_EXPECTED.remedy: Write a path beginning `/`, such as `/auth/ubcshib/callback`; Manifest derives the origin itself.

SPEC_QUOTA_EXCEEDED.summary: A resource, the number of services, or the AI budget is above the project’s quota.
SPEC_QUOTA_EXCEEDED.remedy: Lower what the manifest asks for, or ask an administrator to raise the quota.

SPEC_RESERVED_BLOCK_NOT_EMPTY.summary: `integrations`, `jobs` or `checks` is not empty; schema version 1 reserves each, and each must be empty.
SPEC_RESERVED_BLOCK_NOT_EMPTY.remedy: Leave the block out, or leave it as an empty list.

SPEC_SERVICE_TYPE_UNKNOWN.summary: A service type this platform does not offer.
SPEC_SERVICE_TYPE_UNKNOWN.remedy: Use a service type the hint lists — the ones this platform can provision.

SPEC_UNKNOWN_KEY.summary: A key manifest.yaml does not define at that path.
SPEC_UNKNOWN_KEY.remedy: Remove or rename the key; the hint lists the keys that path accepts.

SPEC_YAML_PARSE_FAILED.remedy: Fix the YAML at the place the message names; YAML indents with spaces, never tabs.
